title: Specialized Tool Pack: Fork 10-15 Wrappers from HexStrike for Tools We Lack
goal: Expand AegisPT runner coverage to specialized areas (binary analysis, forensics, credential cracking, advanced recon) by lifting wrapper logic from 0x4m4/hexstrike-ai (MIT licensed) into our runner contract, with our scope allowlist + audit + intrusive-tier governance added at the runner boundary.
scope: Fork specifically the wrapper logic (CLI invocation + parameter handling) for tools we currently lack. Add proper attribution per MIT license. Implement each as a workers/runners/<name>/runner.py following base.contracts.RunnerExecution shape. Wire into workers/orchestration/tasks.py SUPPORTED_TOOLS, workers/orchestration/findings.py extractor map, and workers/runners/capabilities.json triggers.
generation_reason: HexStrike spike on 2026-05-15 confirmed that their tool-wrapper pattern is trivially liftable - a Volatility wrapper is ~45 lines Flask handler + 20 lines MCP layer. Their server is monolithic (no clean library exists to depend on), but per-tool fork is ~30-60 minutes AI-paced. Forking adds capabilities we don't have without taking architectural lock-in. Spike report: docs/research/2026-05-15-hexstrike-code-spike.md.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement until this package is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Fork only the named 10-15 tools. Do NOT lift the broader HexStrike framework (BrowserAgent, Intelligent Decision Engine, MCP server scaffold). Each tool becomes a standalone AegisPT runner. No HexStrike runtime dependency at any point.
constraints.license_attribution: Each forked runner file MUST contain a header comment crediting 0x4m4/hexstrike-ai (MIT) and the original commit hash. licenses/HEXSTRIKE-MIT.txt must contain a copy of their LICENSE file.
constraints.governance_required: Every forked runner MUST call web_target_value_is_allowed_with_path (or equivalent host-scope check) before executing the tool subprocess. Findings emitted via standard findings.py extractor.
constraints.tier_classification: Each tool gets a default risk_tier (passive | active | intrusive) in capabilities.json matching its destructive potential.

success_criteria: 10-15 new runners exist under workers/runners/ for tools not previously in AegisPT.

Recommended initial set: volatility, foremost, steghide, hydra, john, hashcat, ghidra, radare2, binwalk, exiftool, pwntools, angr, subfinder, amass, katana. Final set may be reduced based on availability of upstream tool binaries on supported OS targets.
Each runner has unit tests covering happy path + scope rejection.
Each runner registered in SUPPORTED_TOOLS, has a findings extractor entry, and a capabilities.json entry.
License attribution header in every forked file. licenses/HEXSTRIKE-MIT.txt present.
AGENT_SYSTEM_MAP.md section 3 updated to list the new runners under Verified-generic.
must_not_touch: api/app/services/auth_discoverer.py (will not exist yet; if it does from #325, do not modify)

acceptance_criteria: Each new runner executes locally if the underlying CLI tool is installed; otherwise emits a clear status=skip with reason.
Scope check rejects out-of-scope targets before subprocess execution.
License attribution header in every forked file.
No HexStrike runtime dependency. No Flask, no fastmcp, no hexstrike imports.

before_promotion: NEXT_TASK.md must contain this task as the single active task.
Phase 2 or later must be reached (auth_discoverer should exist - some of these tools need authenticated sessions).
after_completion: Record in NEXT_TASK.md whether further phase work remains queued; if Mythos backlog completes here, mark NEXT_TASK.md as awaiting operator planning per docs/MYTHOS_PLAN_FINALITY.md Section 7.

out_of_scope: Lifting HexStrike's BrowserAgent (Selenium-based SPA discovery is separate scope).
Running HexStrike as a sidecar service.
Wrapping all 150 tools - this task is the 10-15 highest-value subset.
Re-licensing - all forked content stays MIT-compatible per HexStrike's LICENSE.
